# About the course {.unnumbered}

EXTN 4101 is a three-credit course (1 theory + 2 practical) that builds the communication, organisational and personal skills a biotechnology graduate needs in academic and professional life. The nine lectures and their chapters are listed below.

## Lecture schedule {.unnumbered}

: Lecture schedule of EXTN 4101 {#tbl-schedule .bordered}

| Lecture No. | Topic | Chapter |
|:-----------:|:------|:--------|
| 1 | Group discussion | @sec-gd |
| 2 | Popular science articles | @sec-popsci |
| 3 | Presentation skills | @sec-presentation |
| 4 | Event management | @sec-event |
| 5 | Debate | @sec-debate |
| 6 | Quiz | @sec-quiz |
| 7 | Time management | @sec-time |
| 8 | Oral presentation | @sec-oral |
| 9 | Leadership and motivation | @sec-leadership |

## How the book is organised {.unnumbered}

The nine lectures are grouped into three parts. **Communication Skills** brings together the lectures on group discussion, popular science writing, presentation skills and oral presentation, since all four deal with getting a message across to an audience. **Competitive and Organisational Skills** covers debate, quiz and event management, three activities in which students both participate and organise. **Personal Effectiveness** closes the book with time management, leadership and motivation.

The chapters on *Presentation skills* (@sec-presentation) and *Oral presentation* (@sec-oral) are best read together: the first deals with planning, venue and delivery in general, and the second with the structure and language of a spoken presentation.

## Practical record {.unnumbered}

Each chapter ends its main text with a **Practical assignment** box describing what you should record in your practical notebook after the corresponding practical class. Keep these records neat and up to date; they form part of the internal assessment.
